items.stem: Which security principle is violated when an attacker alters records in a database without authorisation?

options.rationale: Correct: unauthorised alteration of data is a loss of integrity.
Availability concerns whether data/services are accessible, not whether they were altered.
Confidentiality concerns unauthorised disclosure, not alteration.
Non-repudiation concerns proving who performed an action, not the alteration itself.

items.explanation: Correct: unauthorised alteration of data is a loss of integrity.

items.stem: An analyst needs to know exactly which bytes were sent in a suspicious session. Which data source is most appropriate?

options.rationale: Correct: full packet capture preserves complete payloads, allowing byte-level inspection.
NetFlow summarises conversations (addresses, ports, volume) but not payload contents.
Counts show policy hits, not session contents.
DNS logs show name lookups, not the bytes of an arbitrary session.

items.explanation: Correct: full packet capture preserves complete payloads, allowing byte-level inspection.

items.stem: Select TWO items that are classic indicators of compromise (IOCs).

options.text: A known-malicious file hash observed on an endpoint
options.rationale: Correct: a malicious file hash is a well-established IOC.

options.text: Beaconing network traffic to a known command-and-control domain
options.rationale: Correct: periodic callbacks to a known C2 domain are a recognised IOC.
Approved maintenance activity is expected and is not an IOC.

options.text: A user logging in during their normal shift from their usual device
options.rationale: Normal, expected behaviour is a baseline, not an indicator of compromise.

options.text: Successful completion of a routine backup job
options.rationale: A routine backup success is normal operations, not an IOC.

items.explanation: Correct: a malicious file hash is a well-established IOC.
